method: Hand-compiled from published sources. Each figure keeps the sentence it was read from; the checker re-fetches the page and looks for that sentence. kind 'ours' marks a number we measured ourselves, with the script or document that produced it. A bar with no citable figure is left empty; nothing is estimated by us. Bars are scaled within one language only, because languages are counted in different units.

estimated.missing: No published estimate of all Latin editions printed, lost ones included.

scanned.label: at least 65,483 open scans matched to a Latin edition

notes: Of Latin works first written in the Renaissance, 6.7% (4.8 to 8.7%) have an English translation.

figures.what: Latin-language editions in the Universal Short Title Catalogue (all years to 1700), counted in our copy of the USTC data
figures.body: University of St Andrews; count by Source Library
figures.caveat: The USTC records editions known to bibliographers, including some with no surviving copy. Recounted 2026-10-08 by three query paths: 503,360 with Latin as first language, 499,604 of them dated 1450 to 1700, and 29,808 more with Latin as a second language.

figures.what: Distinct open IIIF scans, from seven libraries, that our catalogue join matched to a Latin edition in the USTC
figures.produced_by: Mongo catalog_coverage (scripts/catalog-coverage/build.mjs): distinct iiif_manifest_url where language = Latin, counted 2026-10-08
figures.caveat: A floor. The join matches on title, so one scan is attached to every edition of that title: 251,549 edition rows share these 65,483 scans, which is why this bar counts scans and not editions. In a random sample of 55 matches opened on 2026-10-08, 37 named the same year as the USTC record, about 13 were another edition of the same title, and about 5 were a different work. Scans outside the seven libraries are not counted.

figures.what: Share of Latin works printed 1480 to 1620 with any prior English translation, from a blind stratified sample of 1,000 works judged by two independent search-grounded models
figures.quote: Debiased gap — all-print denominator (1480–1620): 84.9% [82.3–87.3]
figures.caveat: Measured on works, drawn here against editions. The human gold-standard check of the sample is not finished.

figures.unit: share of Byzantine scientific and philosophical texts printed

languages.scope: Books made before 1912, surviving in China

estimated.label: about 200,000 titles, in over 50 million volumes

catalogued.label: close to 200,000 titles in the union catalogue

translated.missing: No published figure. Our own catalogue match finds evidence of English for 65 of 10,141 works in the Kanseki Repository, which is a floor.

notes: Fewer than 40,000 titles have typed text; the rest of the digitised ones are page images only.
Digitised is not the same as open: libraries in China have published images of over 161,000 copies and items free to read online, most of them on the National Library’s platform.
Counted as copies, the national census has registered over 2.7 million, which it says is over 90% of what it expects to find.

figures.what: Ancient books surviving in China: about 200,000 titles in more than 50 million volumes or items

figures.quote: 我国现存古籍约20万种5000多万册（件）
figures.caveat: A commentary in the People's Daily that says 'according to statistics' without naming them. A 2022 report of the census gives 30 million volumes registered.

figures.what: Surviving Chinese ancient books worldwide, as distinct titles, in the union catalogue 中国古籍总目
figures.source_title: 年投资数亿元整理出版古籍

figures.what: Titles digitised in any form; most as page images only, fewer than 40,000 with typed text

figures.what: Copies of pre-1912 books registered by the national census of ancient books; said to be over 90% of the expected Chinese-language total

languages.scope: The Buddhist canon in Tibetan (Kangyur and Tengyur)

figures.quote: to translate and publish the additional 161,800 pages of the Tengyur by the year 2110

figures.what: Texts in 84000's Reading Room catalogue (1,145 Kangyur, 3,396 Tengyur), read from its public catalogue
figures.caveat: The catalogue's own page counts sum to 198,236, a little under 84000's round figure. The catalogue address stopped serving the catalogue by 2026-10-08 (it redirects to 84000.co/reading-room), so this count could not be repeated; it stands as read on 2026-10-01.

figures.what: The Derge Kangyur and Tengyur are scanned in full at the Buddhist Digital Resource Center; we hold all 213 Tengyur volumes from those scans
